Hi Priya,

Thanks for the quick demo last week. Legal at ClearSky reviewed the MSA + Order Form you sent. Attached are our redlines (see RDW-OrderForm-IP-Remediation-draft-v1.docx). Two items are blocking approval from our side: (1) the indemnity carveouts for AI-generated output — we need a firm vendor remediation commitment for any third-party IP claims tied to model outputs; and (2) the ability to recover remediation costs (including outside counsel and forensic reviewers) if the vendor’s model is the source.

Specifically, we asked that Redwood:
- Accept indemnity for third-party IP claims for outputs generated via our dedicated instance (no carveouts for model training dependencies).
- Commit to issue a remediation plan within 5 business days of notice and to reimburse reasonable remediation costs up to actual damages + expenses.

We appreciate your willingness to work through this. Can you confirm Redwood’s position on remediation timelines and whether you will accept a cost-recovery obligation tied to third-party claims?

Best,
Sophia Lane
Senior Counsel, ClearSky Analytics

Thanks Priya — quick read. My initial take from risk/engineering perspective:

1) Remediation SLA: 5 business days to produce a plan is reasonable; 5 business days to fully remediate (e.g., retrain a model) is often unrealistic. Recommend split:
   - Acknowledgement and remediation plan within 5 business days after notice.
   - Technical remediation target: "use commercially reasonable efforts to remediate within 30-60 days depending on root cause; critical mitigations (filters, blocklists) within 7-14 days."

2) Cost recovery: unlimited reimbursement is a no-go. Two compromise structures:
   A) Per-order cap tied to ARR or order value (e.g., up to 2x monthly committed spend)
   B) Escrow/retention trigger: for claims > $X, escrow funds released to cover documented remediation + reasonable counsel fees.

3) Evidence & causation: require customer to provide evidence linking the claim to outputs we served (sample prompts, timestamps, and claimed infringing content). We should also preserve the right to investigate and propose mitigations prior to paying any sums.

I'll draft specific clause language if you want. From infra POV, the engineering team can commit to ship guardrails and keyword blocklists in < 10 business days once PoC confirmed. Model-level fixes will vary.

-Karthik
Head of Product Compliance (note: role for flavor)

From: kimberly_park@redwood.com

Subject: Re: Fwd: Order Form redlines — ClearSky (language suggestions)

Priya/Karthik — suggested legal language below to address ClearSky’s asks while protecting Redwood’s exposure: please review and tell me what goods/services we should tie to caps.

PROPOSED (redline-ready):
1) Notice & Evidence: Customer must provide written notice of the claim including sample prompts, definitive timestamps, and a reasonable evidentiary bundle linking the alleged infringement to outputs produced by Redwood under the Order Form. Redwood shall have the right to inspect log data and perform a technical causation review.

2) Remediation Plan & Timing: Redwood will acknowledge notice within 2 business days and provide a written remediation plan within 5 business days. The remediation plan will (i) detail immediate mitigations (filters/blocklists), (ii) propose a timeline for model-level remediation, and (iii) identify any actions requiring customer cooperation. Redwood shall use commercially reasonable efforts to implement immediate mitigations within 10 business days; model-level changes may require up to 60 days depending on complexity.

3) Reimbursement & Cap: Redwood agrees to reimburse documented, reasonable remediation costs (including third-party forensics and incremental outside counsel reasonably incurred) incurred by Customer up to an aggregate cap equal to the greater of (a) $100,000 or (b) three (3) months of Customer’s committed monthly Order Form spend under this Order Form. Any amounts paid under this section will be offset by amounts recovered from third parties or insurance proceeds.

4) Defense & Subrogation: Redwood retains the right to assume defense of a third-party claim. Redwood will not be liable for any settlement entered into without our prior written consent, which shall not be unreasonably withheld. Customer agrees to cooperate and preserve evidence. Redwood may seek subrogation against any responsible third party.

5) Exclusions: No indemnity for open-source/model training data licensors or claims arising solely from Customer-provided prompts where Customer instructs Redwood to produce content replicating identified materials.

If that language looks OK, I can populate redlines-proposed-v2.docx and send a clean proposal back to ClearSky. Also recommend we propose an escrow-trigger if ClearSky pushes for higher caps.

-Kimberly Park
Senior Counsel, Commercial Contracts

Subject: RE: Order Form redlines — IP remediation & reimbursement mechanics (proposal)

Hi Sophia / Michael — thanks for the redlines and context. We’ve reviewed with product and legal and propose the compromise below (attached as redlines-proposed-v2.docx). Highlights:

- We will acknowledge notice within 2 business days and provide a remediation plan within 5 business days.
- Immediate mitigations (filters, blocklists) targeted within 10 business days; model-level fixes targeted within 60 days depending on root cause.
- Redwood will reimburse documented, reasonable remediation costs up to the greater of $100k or three months’ committed Order Form spend. Amounts will be offset by third-party recoveries or insurance.
- Redwood retains defense rights and subrogation; Customer must provide a reasonable evidentiary bundle linking the claim to outputs from the Order Form.

We believe this strikes the right balance between ClearSky’s need for timely mitigation and our need to limit unbounded exposure, particularly where remediation requires model changes or third-party dependencies.

Please see the attached redline for exact language. If helpful, we can schedule a 30-minute call this week to walk through the operational remediation steps Karthik mentioned. If you can confirm the three-month committed spend amount we’ll plug that into the cap.

Next steps we propose:
1) ClearSky confirms whether the proposed cap formula is acceptable or provides an alternate cap number.
2) If cap acceptable, run a short call to agree on evidence package format and operational contacts.
3) Incorporate agreed language into the final Order Form for signature.

Thanks — look forward to closing this soon.

Best,
Priya Natarajan
Director, Commercial Contracts
Redwood Inference
